Paracetamol is normally metabolised by UGT enzymes to form inactive glucuronide conjugates.  In an overdose, the UGT enzymes become saturated and the paracetamol is metabolised by cytochrome P450 enzymes to form NAPBQI. NAPBQI is a toxic metabolite that is normally deactivated by hepatic glutathione.  In an overdose, the hepatic glutathione is depleted and NAPBQI is able to damage hepatocytes.  n-acetylcysteine (NAC) is a precursor of hepatic glutathione and is used to treat paracetamol overdose.
